text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Helix (enterprise, VPC: eu-west-1) — error rate >5% and 95th latency spike. Paging oncall @Maya Chen. Pager: PD-INC-8912.

Maya Chen: acked. I'm oncall. pulling up graphs now. where's the impact - routing, model errors, or infra?

Samir Patel: looking at proxy logs — 502/504s from the dedicated pool (pool-id: rwd-ded-helix-eu-1). CPU fine but gRPC timeouts between gateway and model frontends.

Nina Gomez: customer impact: Helix reports degraded RPCs for some users in eu-west. They say requests are timing out intermittently. They have a strict SLA. I DM'd Helix SRE to confirm scope.

Helix SRE: Confirmed — ~12% of requests in eu-west for us returning errors since ~08:02 UTC. Business workflows affected (search indexing). We're ready to coordinate a regional move if needed.

Maya Chen: ok. quick triage plan: 1) confirm if this is isolated to dedicated pool; 2) check warm capacity in us-west and eu-central; 3) if warm capacity available, plan traffic-shift + DNS TTL change; 4) preserve cache keys & KV caches.

Raffael Ortiz: hypothesis — intermittent network flaps between eu-west gateways and model workers after a noisy NIC firmware update in that rack. Oncall infra team says some nodes showing kernel network errors.

Alex Wu: network confirms flaps on hostgroup eu-west-gw-3. NOC is isolating hosts. We should prepare a graceful cutover — not a hard failover.

Samir Patel: running runbook check: `rw-infra runbook tenant-regional-failover --tenant helix --from eu-west-1 --to eu-central-1 --dry-run` output shows compatible model variants in eu-central and us-west. cache warmup snapshot available (kv-prefix: helix-prod-v1).

Nina Gomez: Helix wants minimal disruption. They prefer DNS-based shift rather than immediate IP-level reroute. TTL currently 300s. Suggest lowering TTL to 60, perform canary, then full shift.

Maya Chen: agree. Steps: A) reduce DNS TTL to 60 (Helix DNS hosted by their provider) B) spin up additional warm instances in eu-central (reserve 6 units) and start prefix warmup C) update routing policy to prefer eu-central for Helix with fallback to us-west D) monitor errors/latency, roll back if >3% error or 2x latency.

Deploy Bot: Deploy pipeline check: `canary-traffic-shift helix -> eu-central` gate: all checks pass (health, model-compat). Ready to start when you give thumbs.

Maya Chen: @Helix SRE can you patch TTL to 60 now? We want DNS to propagate before shifting any traffic.

Helix SRE: TTL lowered to 60, changes made at 08:17 UTC. Confirmed.

Samir Patel: warmup started: pre-warming model frontends (6 instances) and cache warmup in eu-central. ETA ~7 minutes. Logs: `warmup: 1200/1200 prefixes loaded`.

Raffael Ortiz: NOC finished isolating the noisy hosts in eu-west. They're cordoning racks. But still seeing sporadic packet loss. Prefer failover while isolation completes.

Maya Chen: ok starting canary at 08:26 UTC — shifting 5% of Helix traffic to eu-central. Watch list: error rate, 95th latency, 429s, and backing store timeouts.

Samir Patel: Canary metrics: errors -> 0.8%, latency stable. No cache misses spike.

Nina Gomez: Helix confirms canary transactions for search indexing succeeded. No user-facing failures reported.

Maya Chen: increasing to 25% at 08:30.

Samir Patel: 25% metrics good: errors 1.1% (within baseline), 95th latency +10ms. Proceeding to 60%.

Alex Wu: network note — some eu-west gateways still showing degraded connectivity; keep fallback policy in place.

Maya Chen: moving to 60% at 08:33.

Deploy Bot: Canary -> 60% complete. No gating alerts.

Raffael Ortiz: starting DNS-based cutover final step: update routing policy to route remaining traffic to eu-central.

Maya Chen: doing final 100% shift at 08:36.

Samir Patel: 100% shift completed. Live monitoring: errors dropped to 0.6% globally for Helix, 95th latency back to baseline.

Helix SRE: Observed recovery on our end. We're scaling down retries and watching job backlog clear. Thanks for the smooth cutover. :tada:

Nina Gomez: logged customer-facing incident update. Helix wants an RCA before EOD. I'll open a joint postmortem runbook and include timeline + decisions.

Maya Chen: actions/todo: - open incident ticket PD-INC-8912 (assigned to Maya) - collect logs from eu-west gateways and isolated hosts - preserve warmup snapshots and routing configs - schedule a postmortem with Helix ops at 15:00 UTC.

Raffael Ortiz: devnote: need to blacklist the kernel firmware version on affected hosts and test redeploy of network firmware in canary rack.

Samir Patel: leaving a remediation note: add automated detection for increasing gRPC timeouts between gateway and frontends, run automated warmup to reduce shift latency.

Maya Chen: handing off to next oncall @Samir Patel for monitoring and follow-up. I'll remain reachable for the postmortem.

Deploy Bot: Incident status: mitigated. PD-INC-8912 -> status: mitigated at 08:44 UTC.

Incident Bot: follow-up reminder in #incidents channel in 6 hours for RCA and customer update.

Samir Patel: ack handoff. Adding final notes to the ticket. :thumbsup:
